part.text: The Simulator doesn’t expose touch input through `simctl`, so I’m using an XCTest UI test runner to interact with the already-open app and verify each screen transition.

input.patchText:
*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: project.yml
+name: SimulatorAutomation
+options:
+  bundleIdPrefix: com.example.simulatorautomation
+targets:
+  Host:
+    type: application
+    platform: iOS
+    sources:
+      - path: Host
+    settings:
+      base:
+        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.simulatorautomation.host
+        GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE: YES
+        TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY: "1"
+  UITests:
+    type: bundle.ui-testing
+    platform: iOS
+    sources:
+      - path: UITests
+    dependencies:
+      - target: Host
+    settings:
+      base:
+        PRODUCT_BUNDLE_IDENTIFIER: com.example.simulatorautomation.uitests
+        GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE: YES
+        TEST_TARGET_NAME: Host
+        TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY: "1"
*** Add File: Host/Host.swift
+import SwiftUI
+
+@main
+struct HostApp: App {
+    var body: some Scene {
+        WindowGroup {
+            Text("Automation Host")
+        }
+    }
+}
*** Add File: UITests/AutomationTests.swift
+import XCTest
+
+final class AutomationTests: XCTestCase {
+    func testInspectBluesky() {
+        let app = XCUIApplication(bundleIdentifier: "xyz.blueskyweb.app")
+        app.activate()
+        XCTAssertTrue(app.waitForExistence(timeout: 10))
+        print("BLUESKY_HIERARCHY_BEGIN")
+        print(app.debugDescription)
+        print("BLUESKY_HIERARCHY_END")
+    }
+}
*** End Patch
